_about: Basic facts for the Visual Bible's book pages: who is traditionally held to have written each book, roughly when, to whom, the kind of writing, and its theme as Bible introductions commonly summarize it. Dates are approximate; many are debated, and the ranges and wording say so. 'self' is what the book says of its own author, where it says anything.

Gen.author: Moses, by tradition
Gen.date: Traditionally c. 1440–1400 BC; many scholars date its final form much later
Gen.theme: Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood, and God's promises to Abraham and his family

Exod.author: Moses, by tradition
Exod.self: Says Moses wrote down some of its words (17:14; 24:4; 34:27).
Exod.theme: God rescues Israel from Egypt, makes a covenant with them at Sinai, and comes to dwell among them

Lev.author: Moses, by tradition
Lev.self: Presented as the LORD's words to Moses.
Lev.theme: How a holy God can live among his people: offerings, priests, purity and holiness

Num.author: Moses, by tradition
Num.self: Says Moses recorded the stages of the journey (33:2).
Num.theme: Israel's forty years in the wilderness between Sinai and the edge of the promised land

Deut.author: Moses, by tradition
Deut.self: Presented as Moses' speeches; says Moses wrote this law (31:9).
Deut.date: Traditionally c. 1400 BC; many scholars date it to the 7th century BC
Deut.theme: Moses renews the covenant: love the LORD and keep his commands in the land

Josh.author: Unknown; by tradition, Joshua
Josh.date: Events c. 1400–1350 BC; written later (dates debated)
Josh.theme: Israel enters Canaan and the land is divided among the tribes

Judg.author: Unknown; by tradition, Samuel
Judg.date: Events c. 1350–1050 BC; written in the time of the kings or later
Judg.theme: A cycle of turning from God, oppression, crying out and rescue, when there was no king

Ruth.author: Unknown
Ruth.date: Set in the time of the judges; written in or after David's time
Ruth.theme: Loyal love: a Moabite widow joins Israel and becomes an ancestor of David

1Sam.author: Unknown; by tradition, Samuel with Nathan and Gad
1Sam.theme: Israel moves from judges to kings: Samuel, Saul and the rise of David

2Sam.author: Unknown
2Sam.theme: David's reign: the covenant with David, his sin, and its cost to his house

1Kgs.author: Unknown; by tradition, Jeremiah
1Kgs.self: The book names no author; it cites earlier court records.
1Kgs.date: Events c. 970–850 BC; completed during the exile, c. 560–540 BC
1Kgs.theme: Solomon, the temple, the divided kingdom, and Elijah

2Kgs.author: Unknown; by tradition, Jeremiah
2Kgs.self: The book names no author; it cites earlier court records.
2Kgs.date: Events c. 850–560 BC; completed during the exile
2Kgs.theme: The kings of Israel and Judah until the fall of Samaria and of Jerusalem

1Chr.author: Unknown; by tradition, Ezra
1Chr.self: The book names no author; it cites many sources.
1Chr.theme: Israel's line from Adam, and David's reign with its preparations for the temple

2Chr.author: Unknown; by tradition, Ezra
2Chr.self: The book names no author; it cites many sources.
2Chr.theme: Solomon's temple and the kings of Judah, to the exile and Cyrus's decree

Ezra.author: Ezra, by tradition
Ezra.self: Parts are in Ezra's own voice (7:27–9:15).
Ezra.theme: The return from Babylon, the rebuilding of the temple, and Ezra's teaching of the law

Neh.author: Nehemiah
Neh.date: Events c. 445–430 BC; written c. 430 BC
Neh.theme: Rebuilding Jerusalem's wall and renewing the people's commitment to God

Esth.author: Unknown
Esth.date: Events c. 483–473 BC; written c. 450–330 BC
Esth.to: Jews, especially in the Persian empire
Esth.theme: A Jewish queen and her cousin save their people; the origin of Purim

Job.author: Unknown
Job.date: Setting patriarchal; date of writing unknown and widely debated
Job.theme: Suffering, justice and wisdom: a righteous man's trial and God's answer

Ps.author: Many: David (73 headings), Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses and others
Ps.self: Headings name authors for many psalms; others are anonymous.
Ps.date: From c. 1400 BC (Psalm 90) to after the exile
Ps.theme: Praise, lament, thanks and trust: Israel's prayers to God

Prov.author: Mainly Solomon; also Agur, Lemuel and other sages
Prov.self: Headings name Solomon (1:1; 10:1; 25:1), Agur (30:1) and Lemuel (31:1).
Prov.date: Mostly c. 950 BC; collected into the time of Hezekiah, c. 700 BC (25:1)
Prov.to: The young, and anyone who would be wise
Prov.theme: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom

Eccl.author: “The Teacher, son of David”; by tradition, Solomon
Eccl.self: Calls its author Qohelet, “the Teacher”, son of David, king in Jerusalem (1:1).
Eccl.date: Traditionally c. 935 BC; many scholars date it c. 450–250 BC
Eccl.theme: Life “under the sun” is fleeting; fear God and keep his commands

Song.author: Solomon, by tradition
Song.self: Its title names Solomon (1:1), which may mean “by” or “for” or “about” him.
Song.theme: The love between a man and a woman, celebrated in poems

Isa.author: Isaiah son of Amoz
Isa.date: Ministry c. 740–680 BC; many scholars see later parts from the exile and after
Isa.theme: The Holy One of Israel judges and saves; a coming king and servant, and a new creation

Jer.author: Jeremiah, with his scribe Baruch
Jer.self: Names Jeremiah (1:1) and tells of Baruch writing his words (36:4).
Jer.to: Judah, before and after Jerusalem's fall
Jer.theme: Judgment on Judah's unfaithfulness, and the promise of a new covenant

Lam.author: Unknown; by tradition, Jeremiah
Lam.date: Soon after Jerusalem's fall in 586 BC
Lam.theme: Grief over Jerusalem's destruction, with hope in the LORD's faithful love

Ezek.author: Ezekiel son of Buzi, a priest
Ezek.self: Names Ezekiel and speaks in his voice (1:3).
Ezek.theme: The glory of the LORD leaves Jerusalem and returns; “then you will know that I am the LORD”

Dan.author: Daniel, by tradition
Dan.self: Chapters 7–12 are in Daniel's own voice.
Dan.date: Traditionally 6th century BC; many scholars date it c. 165 BC
Dan.theme: God rules over the kingdoms of the world, and his kingdom will last forever

Hos.author: Hosea son of Beeri
Hos.theme: God's faithful love for unfaithful Israel, pictured in Hosea's marriage

Joel.author: Joel son of Pethuel
Joel.date: Uncertain; proposals range from c. 835 to c. 400 BC
Joel.theme: The day of the LORD, a call to return, and the promise of the Spirit

Amos.author: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa
Amos.theme: Justice: judgment on Israel's injustice and empty worship

Obad.author: Obadiah
Obad.theme: Judgment on Edom, and the kingdom will be the LORD's

Jonah.author: Unknown
Jonah.self: The book names no author; it tells of Jonah son of Amittai.
Jonah.date: Set c. 785–760 BC; date of writing debated
Jonah.theme: God's compassion reaches even Israel's enemies in Nineveh

Mic.author: Micah of Moresheth
Mic.theme: Judgment and restoration; do justice, love faithfulness, walk humbly with God

Nah.author: Nahum of Elkosh
Nah.theme: The fall of Nineveh: the LORD avenges and is a refuge for those who trust him

Hab.author: Habakkuk
Hab.theme: A prophet's questions about injustice; the righteous will live by faithfulness

Zeph.author: Zephaniah, of the line of Hezekiah
Zeph.theme: The day of the LORD, and joy for a humble remnant

Zech.author: Zechariah son of Berechiah
Zech.date: From 520 BC; many date chapters 9–14 later
Zech.theme: Return to the LORD; his coming king and the future of Jerusalem

Mal.author: Malachi
Mal.self: Names Malachi, which also means “my messenger” (1:1).
Mal.to: Jews in Jerusalem after the exile
Mal.theme: Faithfulness to the covenant, and the messenger who will prepare the LORD's way

Matt.author: Matthew, by early church tradition
Matt.theme: Jesus the Messiah, son of David, fulfills the Scriptures and brings the kingdom of heaven

Mark.author: Mark, by early church tradition, drawing on Peter
Mark.theme: Jesus the Son of God, who came to serve and give his life as a ransom

Luke.author: Luke the physician, by early church tradition
Luke.self: Writes in the first person to Theophilus (1:1–4).
Luke.theme: An orderly account of Jesus, the Savior who seeks and saves the lost

John.author: John the apostle, by early church tradition
John.self: Says it was written by “the disciple whom Jesus loved” (21:20–24).
John.to: Not stated; written “so that you may believe” (20:31)
John.theme: Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and believing gives life in his name

Acts.author: Luke, by early church tradition
Acts.self: Addressed to Theophilus, as a second volume (1:1).
Acts.theme: The Spirit spreads the message of Jesus from Jerusalem to Rome

Rom.author: Paul
Rom.self: Names Paul (1:1); Tertius wrote it down (16:22).
Rom.theme: The gospel reveals God's righteousness, received by faith, for Jew and Gentile alike

1Cor.author: Paul, with Sosthenes
1Cor.theme: Unity, holiness, worship and the resurrection, in a divided church

2Cor.author: Paul, with Timothy
2Cor.theme: Strength in weakness: Paul's ministry, reconciliation and generosity

Gal.author: Paul
Gal.theme: Justified by faith, not by works of the law; freedom in Christ

Eph.author: Paul
Eph.self: Names Paul (1:1), writing as a prisoner (3:1).
Eph.to: The saints in Ephesus (and likely other churches)
Eph.theme: God's plan to unite all things in Christ, and the church as his one body

Phil.author: Paul, with Timothy
Phil.theme: Joy in Christ, in every circumstance

Col.author: Paul, with Timothy
Col.theme: Christ is supreme over all, and enough

1Thess.author: Paul, with Silvanus and Timothy
1Thess.theme: Faith, love and hope as they wait for the Lord's coming

2Thess.author: Paul, with Silvanus and Timothy
2Thess.theme: Standing firm and working while waiting for the day of the Lord

1Tim.author: Paul
1Tim.date: c. AD 62–64 (many scholars date it later)
1Tim.theme: Sound teaching and order in God's household, the church

2Tim.author: Paul
2Tim.self: Names Paul (1:1), writing from prison near his death (4:6).
2Tim.date: c. AD 64–67 (many scholars date it later)
2Tim.theme: Guard the gospel and keep going; endure hardship faithfully

Titus.author: Paul
Titus.date: c. AD 62–64 (many scholars date it later)
Titus.theme: Sound teaching that leads to good works

Phlm.author: Paul, with Timothy
Phlm.to: Philemon, and the church in his house
Phlm.theme: Receive Onesimus, once a slave, as a brother

Heb.author: Unknown
Heb.kind: Sermon in the form of a letter
Heb.theme: Jesus is better: the great high priest of a better covenant

Jas.author: James, by tradition the brother of Jesus
Jas.self: Names James, “a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ” (1:1).
Jas.theme: Faith shown by deeds; wisdom for trials, speech and wealth

1Pet.author: Peter the apostle
1Pet.theme: Hope and holy living while suffering as strangers in the world

2Pet.author: Peter the apostle
2Pet.date: c. AD 64–68 (many scholars date it later)
2Pet.to: Those who share the same faith (1:1)
2Pet.theme: Grow in knowledge of Christ; beware false teachers; the Lord's coming is sure

1John.author: John the apostle, by early church tradition
1John.self: The letter names no author; it speaks as eyewitnesses: “what we have heard, seen and touched” (1:1).
1John.to: Believers the writer knew, probably in the province of Asia
1John.theme: Fellowship with God, who is light and love, seen in truth, obedience and love for one another

2John.author: “The elder”; by tradition, John the apostle
2John.to: “The chosen lady and her children” (1): a woman, or a church
2John.theme: Walk in truth and love, and do not welcome deceivers

3John.author: “The elder”; by tradition, John the apostle
3John.theme: Welcome and support those who go out for the truth

Jude.author: Jude, brother of James, by tradition a brother of Jesus
Jude.theme: Contend for the faith against those who distort grace

Rev.author: John
Rev.date: c. AD 95 (some date it c. AD 68)
Rev.to: Seven churches in the province of Asia (1:4)
Rev.kind: Prophecy and apocalyptic vision, in a letter
Rev.theme: The Lamb who was slain reigns; God will make all things new
